steps.content: She leads you to the shop with the tricolor light, pushes open the door, and steps into its warm glow from the dark night.
It's a small hair salon. On the side of the door, where employee nameplates are meant to be hung, there's only one small metal nameplate engraved with a cursive signature:

steps.speaker: Gentle Woman
steps.content: Yes, I'm here.

The woman named Adela looks back at you. You study her face carefully. You don't recognize it, yet it seems familiar at the same time. You're certain that she must exist in some corner of your shattered memories.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Ha, what a funny thing to say. You make it sound as if you've forgotten who I am. This is the <color=#fb9259>second time</color> you've fallen in front of me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Last night</color> I brought you home, and today I brought you into my salon. You keep making a big mess of yourself... and I have to work overtime to tidy you up.
She reaches out and strokes your hair, which had been completely messed up by the monster. She then fixes your crumpled shirt.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: At least you didn't pass out this time. You can change into clean clothes on your own.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: That was the hardest thing for me last night.
She chuckles. You blush, trying not to imagine her changing your clothes.

Now that she mentioned it, the clothes you have on right now are indeed similar to Adela's in style and color. You're a foot away from her, yet totally enveloped by that familiar and reassuring fragrance.
—So the fragrance turned out to be hers. It dispelled your nightmare this morning, and now it's soothing your panic.

You think of the warm water by the bed, the meticulously treated wounds, the hasty but fulfilling breakfast, the washed clothes, and the fact that such a slender girl carried your unconscious body all the way home from the back alley...

options: You're the one who saved me.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Thank you. Sorry for troubling you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: No worries. I'm good at taking care of others. The most important thing was to get you to sleep well.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Now that you came to my little salon, you're my "customer."

As she says this, she brings you to a leather recliner to sit, then puts her hands on your shoulders and slowly presses you to lie down. She does this very gently, yet firmly enough that you can't refuse.
You lie down flat, your head hanging over the small sink. Adela goes to the other side of the sink. She gently supports your head with her soft hands and gazes down into your eyes.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Let's rinse first. Your nerves are too wound up. You need to relax.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Tell me whatever you want to say. Take your time. I always satisfy my customers' needs.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: All right, close your eyes. Don't let the bubbles get in them.
The warm water flows over your head, gently seeping through your hair before forming a downflowing stream.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: How's the water temperature?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: That's good.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sorry. How about now?
The water becomes a bit warmer.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sorry. How about now?
The water becomes a bit warmer.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: If I turn up the temperature even more, you might get scalded. Are you sure?
She asks this as softly as ever, all the while keeping one hand behind your head to feel the water temperature.

options: Yeah, it is a bit too hot.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: All right, then... Oh my, your scalp turned red and a lot of your hair fell out.
You instinctively sit up and look back anxiously at the sink behind you—there's nothing there. You only feel a cold, tingling pain as your scalp readjusts to room temperature.
The woman looks at you with a smile. Her hands are a bit red, but she doesn't seem upset at your mischief at all.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's alright, let me adjust the water to a suitable temperature. Leave it to me, I'll take good care of your hair...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sorry. How about now?
The water becomes a bit cooler.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sorry. How about now?
The water becomes a bit cooler.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I have to add some ice, then. Are you sure about this?
She asks this as softly as ever, all the while keeping one hand behind your head to feel the water temperature.

options: Yeah, it is a bit too cold.

steps.content: You really want to say that, but your teeth are already chattering, and not a word comes out.
She helps you up with a smile and hands you a cup of warm tea. Her hands are a bit blue, but she doesn't seem upset at your mischief at all.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's alright, let me adjust the water to a suitable temperature. I wouldn't want you to catch a cold...
The water flows down your hair to the back of your head. Her soft hands caress your roots with just the right amount of pressure, gradually relaxing your tense and numb scalp.
You hear her soothing voice, as light and bubbly as the foam around your ears. Even the darkness before your eyes starts to mellow out. You have to remind yourself not to fall asleep as you listen.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I saw you around <color=#fb9259>10:30</color> last night.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: On my way home from work, I saw that fog had gathered by the <color=#fb9259>clock tower</color>. There was also a strange red light. So, I went to take a look.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: As soon as I got to the alley, I saw you on the ground, struggling to crawl out, as if trying to escape the dense fog behind you.

options: I remember seeing someone coming over to help me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Yeah, you did see me. Your mouth was also moving, as if you wanted to tell me something.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What did you want to tell me?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You don't remember?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Ha, judging from how your lips moved, that wasn't what you said. Seems like you forgot.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: My memories are jumbled. I can't remember anything from the past.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Everything here is unfamiliar to me. I can't go out and ask for help, nor do I know who to ask for help.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I don't even remember who I am.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: An inspector, perhaps?
You open your eyes to see her smiling at you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's just a guess.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The uniform you changed out of was quite unique. The <color=#fb9259>Minos Bureau of Crisis Control</color>... seems like some kind of secret agency.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I heard from the neighbors that this strange fog elicited quite a bit of attention from the higher-ups, who sent an inspector to investigate. Only an inspector would dare venture into the fog. Plus...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You couldn't even wait for me to get off work before going off to chase the fog... Isn't this the temperament of an inspector?

options: That sounds about right. I'm kinda cool.
Sorry... I made trouble for you again.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I think so, too. "The Great Inspector Who Caught the Mysterious Culprit" is a fitting title for you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Don't worry about it. I think "The Great Inspector Who Caught the Mysterious Culprit" is a fitting title for you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The wash is done. Come, sit here. Let me trim this a bit for you.

<size=31>This time, she ushers you before a mirror, puts you in a barber's chair, then blow-dries your hair. From the reflection, you watch her stare at your hair as she combs it carefully, as if designing a new hairstyle in her mind. Her warm fingertips brush against your ears and neck from time to time.</size>

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Feel free to keep asking, Mr. Inspector. There's an inquisitive passion in your eyes.
steps.female_content: Feel free to keep asking, Ms. Inspector. There's an inquisitive passion in your eyes.

steps.content: How did she know you were looking at her? Was it a woman's intuition? You decide to cast aside your personal questions and ask something more formal.

options: Ask about the mysterious fog that blocked off the street.
Ask about the hair monster in the fog.
Ask about the mysterious lantern in the fog.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The fog in this street has been around long before I moved here.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Usually, it appears only once in a while. I heard that all signals die in there, and people will also lose their way. No one inside the fog can get out, and no one outside can get in.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: But it never lasts long. In one or two hours, or even less, the fog will dissipate and everything will go back to normal.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: But to last more than a day and night without end, and to surround the entire street... Something like this has never happened before.

options: Ask about the hair monster in the fog.
Ask about the mysterious lantern in the fog.

steps.content: You tell her about the rumors you've heard and the battles you've encountered. Adela flashes a puzzled look.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: A monster made of hair? Did it appear in the fog?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I haven't heard of anything like that before... I did hear that "Mad Shears" would appear alongside the fog. But in all the stories, Mad Shears looks like a <color=#fb9259>person</color>, not a monster made of hair...
It must be something that appeared just recently... maybe even <color=#fb9259>today</color>.

options: Ask about the mysterious lantern in the fog.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The neighbors mentioned it before. Seems to be a "new urban legend" that appeared just recently.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I haven't seen it with my own eyes, but others around here have. You can ask around tomorrow. If it led you all the way to me...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Then at least it wasn't "Mad Shears." Maybe it's a kind and cute little fella.

She calmly responds to your questions without resting her hands. Flicking your hair tips to and fro, she shears them off between silver gleams, making you see beauty in her movements.
Your jumbled thoughts are also sorted out little by little. You can clearly see the clues converging to the key questions.

options: The one who attacked me two nights in a row...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Could it be the <color=#fb9259>Mad Shears of the Foggy Night</color>?
...Snap.

The sound of scraping metal grinds sharply from behind your ears. A cold, numbing sensation spreads from the back of your ears to your neck, collarbone, and whole body. You shudder and look instinctively at the mirror...
Those petite barber shears are still dancing lightly, neither sticking to your skin, nor suddenly expanding and piercing towards your throat.
Adela lowers her eyes, smiling gently as she strokes your hair with her left fingertips.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: That's a possibility.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Did you remember something, Mr. Inspector?
steps.female_content: Did you remember something, Ms. Inspector?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: On the first night, I forgot everything that happened before I saw you. And tonight, I was so distracted by those hairs that I didn't see what it looked like.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: But I do remember that pair of <color=#fb9259>shears</color>.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: They were long and freezing cold. I remember that its sound really makes one's skin crawl.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sounds like an eerie urban legend. You like urban legends too, Mr. Inspector?
steps.female_content: Sounds like an eerie urban legend. You like urban legends too, Ms. Inspector?

steps.content: She chuckles.
The barber shears hang less than two centimeters above your neck. This distance is quite intimate.
The cuts are small and the movements are light, clipping away at your hair and tugging at your tense nerves.
Your gaze is completely fixed on the shears in the reflection.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Mr. Inspector, do you know what the residents of this street say about Mad Shears?
steps.female_content: Ms. Inspector, do you know what the residents of this street say about Mad Shears?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: They say that Mad Shears doesn't hurt the prey's body. It only harvests the prey's soul.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: No one knows its true appearance. Mad Shears never misses a target, so it never needs to come back for a retry... Oh, except for you, of course. You're quite special indeed.
The barber shears move faster and faster. You feel its cold gleam edging closer, as if it's going to cut your exposed skin the next second.
The cold, sharp touch feels so real. Every cell is screaming, but you can't tell if they're screaming for you to flee or embrace its approach. Then...
The shears suddenly stop two centimeters from your neck, half-open and gleaming coldly. You glance up and see Adela looking at you in the mirror.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It'll probably still try to come to you amidst the thick fog. Just like <color=#fb9259>tonight</color>.
Clank...!!
You instantly jump up and grab her hand that's holding the shears. By the time you realize what you did, the two of you are frozen face to face before the mirror.
Adela looks at you without struggling. Her gaze grows softer.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...You had the same expression last night.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sorry, I didn't realize how much those shears traumatized you. I'm always quite the dullard.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Forgetting the past makes you quite uneasy, doesn't it? Rest assured, you're not a weakling.
She gently caresses your face with her empty left hand.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You're strong enough to be its match. That's why you got injured all over. No matter what happened in the fog last night, Mad Shears didn't dare to keep chasing you after you left the fog. Nor did it dare to attack you when you were unconscious.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: No, it fled before I came. I'm sure of it. Last night was your victory.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You're very strong. It's just that you can't remember—but that doesn't change who you are.
She gently straightens your shoulders and motions for you to look in the mirror.
Your haircut is done. Adela didn't make any drastic changes. She just trimmed it a little, hiding the gaping cuts made by "Mad Shears" with clever layering. You look quite spruced up.
The terrible snapping hallucinations gradually subside from your ears. You see your familiar old self in the mirror, even though you still can't remember a lot of things from the past.
After calming down, you make up your mind... Whatever your suspicions, this hair stylist just saved you right in front of "Mad Shears". It's a fact that she's not the same person as that monster.
Your tense muscles finally relax. Only then do you remember to let go of her hand. Gazing at her calm face, you actually come to admire this woman a bit.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Everyone was freaking out after the street got blocked off, but you stayed as calm as ever.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You know full well of Mad Shears' existence, yet you still dared to venture out at night alone and save me from the fog. This isn't just an urban legend. You could've gotten hurt.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Yeah. I also lost something in the fog.

options: Do you want to go find it?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Do you think I should worry about it?
She smiles faintly.
Adela ponders for a moment.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: No need. Things are fine the way they are.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: My life is as peaceful as always. I'm content. It should continue like this.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I have work tomorrow, so I can't help you. But you can explore the neighborhood after the sun comes up. The neighbors are all quite kind. Maybe someone has seen you before and can give you some clues.
She sweeps the hair on the floor and tidies up everything swiftly.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: All right, go home now. You should get some rest. You're welcome to stay with me until you regain your memory.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Just relax now. The fog will clear up. You shouldn't worry about it.
